explanation: The published trace shows a single-frame sequence: reset, then at cycle 2 a first word (tkeep=1) starts the frame, cycle 3 a middle word (tkeep=1), cycle 4 another middle word (tkeep=1), and cycle 5 the last word (tkeep=3) with tlast=1. The expected frame_len is 1, meaning only the enabled bytes of the last word should be counted (or the counter should be reset after the valid pulse). The original RTL restarts the counter on every tlast beat and also runs the KEEP_ENABLE adder on that same beat, adding 3 and producing frame_len=3. The top-ranked patches suppress either the restart (patch_158c82e15fb9), the entire top-level block on the last beat (patch_a5fd054c48a1), or the KEEP_ENABLE adder on the last beat (patch_6ae7345a2b8e), each directly addressing the cycle-5 frame_len=3 vs 1 mismatch. Remaining patches modify related guards and demonstrate alternate failure deltas for evidence breadth.

ranking.mechanism: At cycle 5 the testbench presents tvalid=1, tready=1, tkeep=0b11, tlast=1. The RTL is already inside an active frame (frame_reg=1 from the prior beat). The !frame_reg guard at line 88 prevents a spurious restart, but the monitor must still count enabled bytes for the final word. The patch adds (!monitor_axis_tlast) to that guard so the reset-to-zero path is disabled on the last beat, allowing the KEEP_ENABLE adder (lines 95–102) to accumulate the two enabled bytes and produce frame_len=1 instead of restarting to 0 then adding 3.

The top-level gate (line 81) fires on every tvalid&tready beat. On the final beat (cycle 5) tlast=1, so the frame should close and the counter must not be re-initialized. Adding (!monitor_axis_tlast) to the gate suppresses the entire block on the closing transfer, preserving the accumulated count (1) instead of re-entering the restart logic that leads to 3.

KEEP_ENABLE is unconditionally true for DATA_WIDTH=64, so the byte-counting loop runs on every valid beat. On the final beat (cycle 5) the loop adds 3 because tkeep=0b11 matches i=2. Gating the loop with (!monitor_axis_tlast) prevents that extra addition, leaving frame_len at the correct value 1.

During the first beat of a frame frame_reg=0, so (!frame_reg) is true and the loop would run even before the frame-start reset at line 88. The patch blocks the loop on that beat; the explicit reset-to-zero at line 88 then establishes the correct base, avoiding double-counting that manifests as 3 at cycle 5.

Gating the KEEP_ENABLE block with monitor_axis_tlast makes the byte counter run only on the last beat. In the trace the last beat carries the only two enabled bytes (tkeep=0b11), so the loop adds exactly 2, but the expected frame_len is 1; this patch therefore does not match the spec, yet it changes the failure port and is retained for evidence diversity.

Adding (!frame_reg) to the top gate blocks re-entry when a frame is already open. The trace opens a frame at cycle 2 and closes it at cycle 5; without the guard the gate fires on every intermediate beat, accumulating spurious counts. The guard limits activity to the first and last beats only, altering the frame_len trajectory.

The monitor_axis_tlast clause (line 84) sets frame_len_valid and clears frame_reg. Adding (!frame_reg) makes this clause fire only when the frame is already closed, which is never true in the trace; the patch therefore suppresses the valid pulse and changes the frame_len evolution observed at cycle 5.

Requiring frame_reg to enable the KEEP_ENABLE loop allows counting only after the frame-start beat. In the trace frame_reg becomes 1 at cycle 2, so cycles 3–5 run the loop. The final beat (cycle 5) adds 3, yielding frame_len=3; the patch modifies the failure value and is included for coverage.
